question: An 80-year-old man is scheduled for elective bowel resection. Pre-operative assessment reveals MMSE 22/30, serum albumin 28 g/L, and he takes 7 regular medications. Which combination of findings places him at HIGHEST perioperative risk?

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Incorrect. While polypharmacy increases risk, the combination of cognitive impairment plus hypoalbuminaemia is a more potent risk predictor for post-operative complications in the elderly.

Correct. Cognitive impairment predicts post-operative delirium, and hypoalbuminaemia (marker of malnutrition and frailty) predicts poor wound healing and infection — together they represent the highest combined risk in geriatric surgical patients.
Incorrect. Chronological age alone is a weaker predictor than functional and nutritional status. 'Biological age' (frailty, cognition, albumin) matters more.
Incorrect. Hypoalbuminaemia is an important risk factor but the combination with cognitive impairment (delirium risk) is the highest-risk pairing.

overallFeedback.feedback: In geriatric surgical risk, cognitive impairment (delirium risk) + malnutrition (albumin <35 g/L = frailty marker) together confer the greatest peri-operative risk.
Correct. Cognitive impairment + hypoalbuminaemia is the highest-risk combination — predicts post-operative delirium, poor healing, and prolonged recovery.
